## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # Vectors
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Geometric vectors and directions
//  - Integer vectors
//  - Numeric tuples

//==
// # Geometric vectors and directions
//
// Displacements and directions in 2D, 3D, and N-dimensional space
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclidean_vector). Points (`points.types.plato`) are
// positions; these geometric vectors are the differences between them, and a
// Direction is a vector carrying a unit-length invariant.
//
// Discoverability: the concrete operations for Vector2D and
// Vector3D — Normalize, Dot, Cross, Length/LengthSquared,
// Add/Subtract/Multiply/Divide, Reflect, Transform — are declared on the
// intrinsic hub in `intrinsics.library.plato`, not restated here. The
// interface-generic helpers (Distance, DistanceSquared, projection/rejection,
// AngleBetween, and the safe `NormalizeOr` / Direction factories) live in
// `numeric-structures.library.plato`.

// A displacement or direction in 2D space.
type Vector2D
    implements IVector
{
    X: Number;
    Y: Number;
}

// A displacement or direction in 3D space.
type Vector3D
    implements IVector
{
    X: Number;
    Y: Number;
    Z: Number;
}

// An N-dimensional vector with runtime-determined arity.
// VectorN is the one IVector implementor whose components are not its fields, so
// the writer's At/Count synthesis has to delegate to the field rather than count
// fields. It does: verified by emitting and running the code, a 5-component
// VectorN reports Count == 5 and At(2) == 3. The generic bodies in
// numeric-structures.library.plato that read Count/At as the component surface are
// correct here.
//
// This works because the field is spelled Array<Number>: the writer delegates
// Count/At to any IIndexable-providing field type, not only to fields named
// "Array". Keep the field's type IIndexable-providing if this declaration is
// ever reshaped.
//
// VectorN's intrinsic vector operators (Add, Subtract, Magnitude, Zero, ...) are
// not yet filled; the interface-generic bodies below therefore compute only at the
// Number instantiation today.
type VectorN
    implements IVector
{
    Components: Array<Number>;
}

// A 2D direction: a Vector2D with the invariant that its magnitude is one
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unit_vector). The invariant is a promise of
// intent, not a runtime proof: an arbitrary Vector2D may violate unit length
// after a non-rigid transform or manual construction. Construct one via
// normalization of a non-zero displacement — the validated factories
// `FromVector` / `TryFromVector` (and the explicitly unsafe
// `FromVectorUnchecked`) in `numeric-structures.library.plato`; zero input
// is undefined. Check unit length with `IsUnit` (algebra.library.plato) for
// diagnostics.
type Direction2D
    implements IValue
{
    Vector: Vector2D;
}

// A 3D direction: a Vector3D with the invariant that its magnitude is one
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unit_vector).
// The invariant is a promise of intent, not a runtime proof: an arbitrary
// Vector3D may violate unit length after a non-rigid transform or manual
// construction. Construct one via normalization of a non-zero displacement —
// the validated factories `FromVector` / `TryFromVector` (and the explicitly
// unsafe `FromVectorUnchecked`) in `numeric-structures.library.plato`; zero
// input is undefined. Check unit length with `IsUnit`
// (algebra.library.plato) for diagnostics.
type Direction3D
    implements IValue
{
    Vector: Vector3D;
}

//==
// # Integer vectors
//
// Fixed-arity tuples of whole-number components: pixel offsets, grid steps, and
// voxel offsets. They implement IValue and IHashable rather than the IVector
// interface, so no norm, normalization, or component-wise division surface is
// implied — lift them into a Number tuple when real
// arithmetic is wanted.

// A pair of whole-number components: pixel offsets, grid steps.
type IntegerVector2
    implements IValue, IHashable
{
    X: Integer;
    Y: Integer;
}

// A triple of whole-number components: voxel offsets, 3D grid steps.
type IntegerVector3
    implements IValue, IHashable
{
    X: Integer;
    Y: Integer;
    Z: Integer;
}

// A quadruple of whole-number components.
type IntegerVector4
    implements IValue, IHashable
{
    X: Integer;
    Y: Integer;
    Z: Integer;
    W: Integer;
}

//==
// # Numeric tuples
//
// The low-level intrinsic tier of the IVector family: fixed-arity tuples of
// Numbers with component-wise arithmetic, mapped directly onto each backend's
// native vector type (System.Numerics, vecN, floatN). Naming rule: a bare number
// counts components (Number3, Tuple3, IntegerVector3); a D suffix means the type
// lives in that-dimensional space (Vector3D, Point3D, Ray3D).
//
// Discoverability: the concrete per-component operations for
// Number2/3/4/8 — Normalize, Dot, Length/LengthSquared,
// Add/Subtract/Multiply/Divide, Transform — are declared on the intrinsic hub in
// `intrinsics.library.plato`, not restated here.

// A pair of Numbers: the low-level intrinsic 2-tuple.
type Number2
    implements IVector
{
    X: Number;
    Y: Number;
}

// A triple of Numbers: the low-level intrinsic 3-tuple.
type Number3
    implements IVector
{
    X: Number;
    Y: Number;
    Z: Number;
}
```
